It found that at the same MVPA levels, HbA1c was significantly lower in Non-Hispanic White adults compared to Non-Hispanic Black and Mexican American adults, suggesting that PA benefits vary by race/ethnicity.

rank.reason: Focuses on clinical OSA screening using audio signals, not mechanistic or computational sleep regulation modeling in animals; peripheral to core interests.

pubmed:42691826.summary: This systematic review evaluated studies using audio signals (e.g., smartphone, microphone) and machine learning to detect moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) in adults. Among 15 included studies, six reported both sensitivity and specificity of at least 80%, indicating that audio-based screening is plausible and sufficiently accurate.

rank.reason: Unrelated to sleep neuroscience; addresses dermatologic conditions and associated mental health in underserved populations.

pubmed:42694142.summary: This narrative review examined the relationship between pediatric dermatologic conditions, mental health outcomes, and healthcare disparities in underserved US populations, synthesizing studies from 2015 to 2025. It found consistent associations between chronic skin diseases (e.g., atopic dermatitis, acne) and psychosocial burden, and identified barriers such as delayed specialty care; teledermatology may improve access but faces telehealth disparities.

rank.reason: Involves OSA as a covariate but focuses on retinal vascular changes in humans; not central to sleep homeostasis or animal EEG/EMG.

pubmed:42694659.summary: In a retrospective study of 31 patients with chronic NAION, DVA showed reduced arterial dilation amplitude in affected eyes compared to controls, and lower arteriovenous ratio in both eyes, indicating impaired retinal arterial function. OSA was present in 51% but not associated with DVA parameters.

rank.topic: GenAI use and mental health in students
rank.reason: Associates GenAI use with sleep problems in students, but is a cross-sectional survey with no mechanistic or animal model implications.

pubmed:42694124.summary: This cross-sectional study of 1,872 Chinese university students identified four profiles of generative AI (GenAI) use and mental health risk: low-risk adaptive users (39.9%), anxiety-prone dependent users (25.7%), sleep-disrupted overusers (19.8%), and high-risk dysregulated users (14.6%). Higher health literacy and self-regulated learning were associated with lower-risk profiles, and network analysis identified central nodes such as loss of control, academic worry, and delayed bedtime.

rank.reason: Mentions sleep as a lifestyle factor in ADHD management, but is a general practice review unrelated to sleep regulation neuroscience.

pubmed:42692445.summary: This review outlines evidence-based non-pharmacological ADHD management strategies, including psychological approaches like CBT, behavioral parent training, and lifestyle interventions such as sleep and exercise. It emphasizes the role of general practitioners in psychoeducation and referral.

rank.reason: Directly addresses molecular mechanisms of sleep need, intensity, and circadian timing using mouse EEG/EMG, highly relevant to sleep homeostasis and circadian interactions.

pubmed:42696311.summary: The study generated isoform-selective SIK3 knock-in mice and PKA-phosphorylation site mutants to dissect isoform-specific functions in sleep and circadian regulation. They found that the 150 kDa SIK3 isoform controls wakefulness at dark onset and circadian period, while the 70 kDa isoform affects NREM sleep delta power, and alanine substitution at T469 or S551 produced hypersomnia.

rank.topic: Food intake and sleep in humans
rank.reason: Human naturalistic mobile EEG study, but focus on food intake, not core sleep regulation mechanisms or animal models; low transferability.

biorxiv:10.64898/2026.08.31.748421.summary: This naturalistic study used mobile EEG and questionnaires in healthy participants to examine bidirectional time-lagged within-person associations between sleep and food intake, finding that later last meal timing predicted later sleep onset, longer fasting to sleep predicted reduced total sleep time and efficiency, and later sleep shifted next-day eating later. It concluded that links are primarily timing-related, with no negative effect of large, late, or satiating meals on sleep quality.

rank.reason: Circadian regulators in osteoclasts, unrelated to sleep neuroscience despite EEG/EMG not involved; tangential circadian link only.

pubmed:42696159.summary: This study examined osteoclast-specific deletion of both Per1 and Per2 in mice and found suppression of osteoclastogenesis and increased bone mass in males, opposite to Per1 single knockout. Transcriptomic and ChIP analyses indicate PER1 and PER2 regulate osteoclastogenesis through coordinated control of innate immunity genes with opposing effects.

rank.topic: Caffeine and circadian genes in mice
rank.reason: Uses mice and measures circadian gene expression and behavior, but focus is caffeine effects, not sleep homeostasis or EEG/EMG; moderately relevant to circadian regulation.

pubmed:42695266.summary: This study investigated age-dependent effects of caffeine on body weight, behavior, and circadian gene expression in young and mature male mice. Caffeine improved balance and coordination, altered circadian gene expression (Clock, Bmal1, Per2, Cry1, Cry2) in brain and Neuro 2a cells, and modulated adenosine receptor levels with age differences.

rank.reason: EEG functional connectivity in Alzheimer's and mild cognitive impairment with VR, completely outside sleep/wake regulation in animals; no relevance.

pubmed:42696736.summary: This exploratory single-session repeated-measures EEG study in 60 older adults (AD, MCI, NC) found that immersive VR exposure altered EEG functional network organization state-dependently, with higher global efficiency in AD than NC at baseline but no significant group differences during VR, and within-group increases in efficiency from pre-VR to VR in NC and pre-VR to post-VR in MCI. The study demonstrates feasibility of VR-EEG for characterizing network responsiveness but provides no confirmatory evidence of causality or therapeutic efficacy.

rank.reason: Provides a detailed protocol for synchronizing cells and analyzing circadian clock gene expression, potentially transferable to mechanistic circadian studies.

pubmed:42695613.summary: This methods paper presents a detailed protocol for synchronizing cultured mHypoE-42 hypothalamic cells using serum shock, followed by time-course sampling and analysis of circadian clock gene expression via qRT-PCR with appropriate statistical methods. The protocol aims to standardize in vitro circadian experiments for reproducibility.

rank.reason: Review on antipsychotic effects on sleep in psychiatric patients, not animal models or mechanistic sleep regulation; low relevance.

pubmed:42695067.summary: This narrative review summarizes the neurobiology of sleep and receptor-based hypotheses of how lurasidone, an antipsychotic with low sedation liability, may affect sleep architecture, concluding that direct human evidence for sleep architecture modification is limited and that lurasidone's sleep-related benefits beyond psychiatric symptom improvement remain unproven. Most important contribution is the synthesis of available evidence and identification of gaps, including need for long-term polysomnography and circadian biomarker studies.

rank.reason: Examines Rev-Erbα circadian regulator in epilepsy with EEG, but centered on epilepsy and brain regions, not sleep homeostasis or recovery; still relevant due to circadian and EEG methods.

pubmed:42695257.summary: This study examined Rev-Erbα expression in the medial prefrontal cortex, hippocampus, and occipital visual cortex of mice with acute and chronic epilepsy, and tested the effects of the Rev-Erbα agonist SR9009. They found that SR9009 reduced seizure activity, abnormal EEG discharges, and improved anxiety-like behavior and spatial memory, suggesting antiepileptic and neuroprotective roles.

rank.reason: EEG theta-beta ratio in ASD during attention tasks, no connection to sleep regulation or circadian rhythms; irrelevant.

pubmed:42695260.summary: This study analyzed EEG theta-beta ratio (TBR) in children with ASD and TD during multiple object tracking tasks under happy/sad prosody, finding higher TBR in ASD across all brain regions and an interaction between attention level and emotion for global and temporal TBR, with temporal TBR differing between emotions during high-load tracking. It provides evidence for altered attention-emotion interaction in ASD, particularly in temporal regions.

rank.reason: Focuses on pharmacological interaction with hypoxia and sleep deprivation, not sleep regulation mechanisms; peripheral to core interests.

pubmed:42696933.summary: In a mouse model combining acute hypobaric hypoxia and sleep deprivation, modafinil improved cognitive deficits but its pharmacokinetics were altered, with delayed elimination associated with biphasic Cyp3a11 regulation and progressive liver injury.

rank.reason: Review of human REM phasic autonomic activity, relevant to REM physiology but focuses on humans and overview, not core animal models or regulatory dynamics.

pubmed:42697773.summary: This review catalogs phasic autonomic activities during human REM sleep, including pupillary, cardiovascular, respiratory, and reproductive changes, and discusses how they cluster with rapid eye movements and muscle twitches.

rank.reason: Directly addresses spindle dynamics and plasticity induction, methodologically relevant to spectral dynamics and mechanistic sleep neuroscience, though human and non-invasive.

biorxiv:10.64898/2026.09.01.748506.summary: The study tested EEG-triggered TMS targeting different sleep spindle states in sleeping participants and found that only spindle-trough stimulation induced robust long-term depression-like motor cortical plasticity, with no consistent changes from other phases.

rank.reason: Clinical oncology study using wearable sleep metrics, far from basic sleep regulation in animals; peripheral.

pubmed:42697086.summary: In a prospective cohort of 1,000 colorectal cancer patients, delayed perioperative immunocircadian recovery was associated with higher circulating tumor DNA-based minimal residual disease positivity and worse disease-free and overall survival, adding prognostic value beyond conventional factors.

rank.reason: Clinical biomarker meta-analysis in REM behavior disorder, not relevant to basic sleep homeostasis or animal models.

pubmed:42696950.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis found that visual assessment of dorsolateral nigral hyperintensity on MRI has high specificity but moderate sensitivity for differentiating idiopathic REM sleep behavior disorder from healthy controls, and it correlates with abnormal dopamine transporter imaging.

rank.reason: Human psilocybin study with acute/sub-acute EEG changes; not directly related to sleep homeostasis or sleep regulation in animal models, but explores spectral dynamics and recovery, tangentially relevant.

pubmed:42698232.summary: In a double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial with 20 healthy participants, psilocybin acutely reduced alpha/beta EEG power and increased gamma-band signal diversity, which correlated with acute psychological effects; at 24 hours, reduced delta/theta power correlated with positive life changes at 4 weeks, suggesting a sub-acute 'afterglow' distinct from acute psychological intensity.

rank.reason: EEG decoding of audiovisual spatial representations; no sleep component, unrelated to research focus.

pubmed:42697719.summary: Using EEG and cross-generalized inverted encoding models in a ventriloquist task, the study found that spatial representations of auditory and visual modalities remain independent early, but cross-modal biases emerge from ~200 ms onward, with auditory representations biased before visual, indicating late feedback-driven integration.

rank.reason: Clinical trial of acupuncture for chronic insomnia; relevant to insomnia but human clinical, not mechanistic or animal-based, low transferability to sleep regulation research.

pubmed:42697250.summary: In a randomized controlled trial of 201 patients with chronic insomnia, 6- and 8-week acupuncture courses produced significantly greater improvements in insomnia severity than a 4-week course, but extending treatment from 6 to 8 weeks provided limited additional benefit for core sleep outcomes.

rank.reason: TMS-EEG study of acute alcohol effects; potentially relevant to spectral dynamics but no sleep context, methodological transfer limited.

pubmed:42698349.summary: In 34 healthy adults, acute alcohol intoxication decreased TMS-evoked EEG potential amplitudes (P30, N45, P60, N100, P180) and global mean field power in a time-dependent and region-specific manner, with effects most prominent in frontal and central regions, indicating dynamic modulation of cortical excitability.

rank.topic: Temperature mattress and sleep in athletes
rank.reason: Field study on temperature-controlled mattress effects on subjective sleep; human athletes, no mechanistic insights, low relevance to animal sleep neuroscience.

pubmed:42694933.summary: In a 14-night parallel-group field study with 32 elite male Australian Rules football athletes, use of a temperature-controlled mattress cover led to significant improvements in subjective sleep quality, total sleep time, and global sleep scores compared to controls, suggesting it may be a promising noninvasive strategy for improving perceived sleep.

rank.reason: Method for obtaining brain tissue from SEEG electrodes for omics; could transfer to longitudinal recordings but not sleep-specific, some methodological relevance.

biorxiv:10.64898/2026.09.01.747265.summary: This paper presents a method for collecting epileptic brain tissue from stereoelectroencephalography (SEEG) electrodes for transcriptomic and proteomic analyses. The method yielded high-quality RNA and proteins from six patients, identified inflammatory activation in the epileptogenic zone, and showed concordant transcriptomic and proteomic findings.

rank.reason: Large-scale genetic study of circadian feeding rhythms; relevant to circadian-homeostatic interactions and quantitative trait analysis, highly transferable concepts and methods.

biorxiv:10.64898/2026.09.01.748529.summary: This study quantified circadian feeding rhythmicity in pigs using 40.5 million feed intake records from automated systems, finding it heritable (0.53-0.57) and associated with improved feed efficiency and lower day-to-day variability. Genome-wide association testing identified a locus on chromosome 4 explaining up to 5.3% of phenotypic variance, overlapping the OPRK1 and NPBWR1 genes.

rank.reason: Decoding specific memories from human neurons before/after sleep; directly relevant to sleep-dependent memory processing and role of NREM sleep, highly relevant mechanism.

biorxiv:10.1101/2025.07.01.662486.summary: This study developed a transformer neural network model trained on intracranial neuronal spikes from a single viewing of an audiovisual episode to decode specific concepts during memory recall in individual participants. The model successfully decoded concepts, and analysis revealed distinct contributions from medial temporal lobe and frontal cortex before and after sleep, suggesting a shift in neural information distribution across wake/sleep cycles.

rank.reason: Diagnostic study of REM sleep parameters in narcolepsy; human clinical, methodologically relevant to sleep scoring but limited to clinical diagnosis.

pubmed:42694690.summary: This clinical study evaluated REM sleep-related indicators for diagnosing narcolepsy subtypes against other hypersomnias, using data from 206 patients. Daytime REM sleep duration and any REM sleep without atonia (RSWA) during MSLT showed high AUC values (0.865-0.948) and good sensitivity/specificity for distinguishing NT1 and NT2, with co-occurrence of REM-related symptoms providing high specificity for NT1.

rank.topic: Maternal circadian disruption and offspring disease
rank.reason: Narrative review on maternal circadian disruption effects on offspring cardiometabolic disease; tangentially related via circadian disruption, but broad and clinical.

pubmed:42694455.summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence that maternal circadian disruption during pregnancy can program offspring susceptibility to diabetes and cardiovascular complications via the clock-metabolic-oxidative stress axis, and discusses chronotherapeutic strategies like melatonin as potential interventions.
keywords: developmental origins of health and disease

rank.topic: E/I balance linking sleep and ASD
rank.reason: Review proposing E/I balance framework linking sleep disturbances and ASD; covers synaptic homeostasis and network rebalancing, conceptually relevant to sleep regulation mechanisms.

pubmed:42694601.summary: This review synthesizes evidence from multiple methodologies to propose a bidirectional framework linking sleep disturbances and autism spectrum disorder (ASD) via excitation/inhibition (E/I) imbalance. It suggests that E/I-related vulnerability may impair sleep, and sleep disruption may exacerbate ASD symptoms through synaptic homeostasis alterations.

rank.reason: M/EEG study on neural subspaces in working memory; no sleep component, not relevant to sleep regulation.

biorxiv:10.64898/2026.08.31.748237.summary: The study used M/EEG recordings from healthy humans performing a visual working memory task to show that neural subspace geometry changes dynamically with task demands: prioritization expands and de-prioritization shrinks subspaces, with orthogonality increasing under high cognitive load, driven by aperiodic activity and delta/theta oscillations.

rank.reason: MRI study of CSF-vascular changes in AD; mentions slow-wave sleep speculation but no direct sleep measurement, weakly relevant.

pubmed:42695591.summary: This study used phase-contrast and 4D-flow MRI to quantify CSF and blood flow in Alzheimer's disease, finding altered CSF-vascular associations suggesting glymphatic involvement and proposing these metrics as a non-invasive biomarker framework for early AD detection.

rank.reason: Scoping review of EEG/ECG in music listening; no sleep component, unrelated to sleep neuroscience.

pubmed:42693627.summary: A scoping review of 18 papers on simultaneous EEG and ECG during passive music listening in healthy adults found heterogeneous findings and methodological inconsistencies, with limited direct brain-heart coupling evidence, highlighting the need for standardization.

rank.topic: HRV during short EEG in clinical patients
rank.reason: Human clinical study of autonomic function during routine EEG; minimal overlap with animal sleep homeostasis or spectral dynamics.

pubmed:42701827.summary: The study measured heart rate variability (HRV) in 103 patients undergoing routine short-term EEG and found reduced HRV compared to normal values, indicating that a normal EEG does not predict normal HRV. HRV was stable across wakefulness and sleep stages, suggesting that measuring HRV during the first five minutes of EEG could provide useful prognostic information.

rank.reason: Surgical case report on rare epilepsy; not relevant to sleep regulation or basic neuroscience.

pubmed:42699933.summary: This case report describes a 25-year-old patient with mild malformation of cortical development with oligodendroglial hyperplasia and epilepsy (MOGHE) in the right temporal lobe, who had a delayed diagnosis and extensive epileptogenic areas. After surgical resection of the right temporal and frontal regions, the patient experienced only occasional minor focal seizures over 14 months, suggesting that larger resection may improve outcomes in delayed MOGHE cases.

rank.reason: Human observational systematic review on circadian disruption and liver disease; only tangential circadian-homeostatic relevance.

pubmed:42701454.summary: This systematic review of 24 human observational studies found that shift work showed the most consistent associations with MASLD, while chronotype, sleep timing, and other circadian exposures had less consistent or limited evidence. Heterogeneity and confounding preclude causal conclusions, and prospective studies with objective circadian phenotyping are needed.

rank.topic: Social jetlag and inhibitory control in young adults
rank.reason: Computational modeling of behavioral inhibition in humans; useful concept of circadian misalignment but not core interest.

pubmed:42700591.summary: This study examined the association between social jetlag and inhibitory control in healthy young adults using the horse-race model. Higher social jetlag predicted longer stop-signal reaction times and greater race model values, indicating delayed inhibition processes, while raw reaction times showed no significant association, highlighting the value of computational modeling.

rank.topic: Maternal circadian disruption and offspring outcomes
rank.reason: Rat model of constant-light-induced circadian disruption across pregnancy/lactation; links circadian disruption to neurobehavior but not sleep homeostasis or EEG.

pubmed:42701165.summary: This study investigated the effects of maternal circadian rhythm disruption during distinct reproductive stages (pre-pregnancy, pregnancy, lactation) on male rat offspring. Offspring from pre-pregnancy and pregnancy disruption showed increased anxiety- and depressive-like behaviors, altered hippocampal CA1 morphology, and molecular changes, while lactation disruption had fewer effects, suggesting stage-specific impacts on neurodevelopment.

rank.topic: Dynamic model of weekly sleep timing
rank.reason: Integrates two-process model and decision-making to explain endogenous social jetlag; directly relevant to quantitative models of sleep regulation and circadian-homeostatic interaction.

pubmed:42698611.summary: The authors developed a dynamic model integrating the two-process model of sleep regulation with time-allocation decisions, showing that weekly sleep patterns including social jetlag can emerge endogenously from behavioral tradeoffs over scarce workday leisure, without requiring fixed wake times or bedtimes. The model reproduces shorter workday sleep, weekend recovery sleep, and later free-day midsleep, and brings simulated patterns closer to empirical estimates when realistic constraints are added.

rank.topic: Chronic stress and approach motivation from resting EEG
rank.reason: Human resting EEG correlates of stress; peripheral to sleep research, although delta/theta bands mentioned but not in sleep context.

pubmed:42701311.summary: In 60 undergraduates, perceived chronic stress showed a U-shaped relationship with resting-state EEG measures of approach motivation, including alpha frontal asymmetry and delta/theta power. This nonlinear pattern suggests that both low and high stress enhance baseline approach motivation, while moderate stress reduces it.

rank.reason: Human longitudinal study linking sleep fragmentation via actigraphy to depression; clinical population, not animal mechanistic research.

pubmed:42698909.summary: Using latent profile analysis in 306 adults, a profile characterized by high inflammation and sleep disturbances predicted 9-year major depressive disorder severity beyond baseline. This suggests that a person-centered neuroimmune profile may serve as a distal risk factor for depression.

rank.topic: Aβ pathology and sleep apnea in 5XFAD mice
rank.reason: Mouse model of AD with respiratory measures; touches on sleep-disordered breathing but not directly on sleep homeostasis or EEG.

pubmed:42700451.summary: In 5XFAD mice, amyloid beta plaque deposition in brainstem respiratory regions was associated with increased spontaneous apnoeas and blunted hypoxic and hypercapnic ventilatory responses, indicating chemosensory dysfunction. This suggests a link between Aβ pathology and respiratory deficits in Alzheimer's disease models.

rank.reason: Cardiovascular molecular study on OSA-related intermittent hypoxia; no sleep EEG or regulation relevance.

pubmed:42701168.summary: This study examined the effect of alamandine on atrial fibrillation induced by chronic intermittent hypoxia in rats. Alamandine reduced atrial fibrillation susceptibility and attenuated endoplasmic reticulum stress and pyroptosis-related protein expression, suggesting its potential as a therapeutic agent for AF.

rank.topic: Smartphone sensing vs actigraphy in bipolar youth
rank.reason: Methodological comparison of sleep measurement in humans; potential transfer of wearable sensing but not core animal work.

pubmed:42700485.summary: This study compared smartphone-based mobile sensing with actigraphy for sleep metrics in youth with bipolar disorder, finding strong agreement for sleep timing and duration, with the strongest agreement for midsleep (RMSE = 14.8 minutes). Mobile sensing slightly overestimated sleep duration and underestimated wake after sleep onset, but was sensitive to the presence of nocturnal wakefulness, supporting its potential for scalable monitoring.

rank.topic: Carbohydrate intake and sleep in female athletes
rank.reason: Sports nutrition intervention examining sleep metrics; peripheral to researcher's interests.

pubmed:42700960.summary: This exploratory study investigated the effects of higher (6 g/kg/d) versus lower (3 g/kg/d) carbohydrate intake on training adaptations, health, and sleep in female rugby athletes over a 7-week preseason. Despite increasing energy availability, the intervention did not significantly alter training adaptations, physique, or biochemical markers, but reduced sleep duration on training nights.

rank.topic: Emotional eating and sleep disturbances in adolescents
rank.reason: Epidemiological longitudinal study on eating and sleep; weak theoretical link to sleep regulation.

pubmed:42700711.summary: In 3216 Generation R adolescents, no overall within-person cross-lagged associations between emotional eating and sleep disturbances were found, but concurrent co-occurrence was observed at age 18. Subgroup analyses showed that emotional eating at age 14 predicted sleep disturbances at age 18 in European-origin and low-overweight-risk youth.

rank.topic: Sleep and brain volumes in NMOSD
rank.reason: Human neuroimmunological disorder with actigraphy and MRI; explores brain-sleep associations but far from core.

pubmed:42700625.summary: This exploratory cross-sectional study assessed sleep and brain volumes in AQP4-IgG-positive NMOSD, finding longer time in bed and total sleep time by actigraphy, no differences in sleep efficiency or wake after sleep onset, and worse subjective sleep disturbance. Volume reductions were seen in hippocampal subfields and corpus callosum segments, but no volume-sleep associations survived correction.

rank.reason: Clinical bariatric study; sleep apnea only as comorbidity outcome; no mechanistic insight relevant to sleep regulation research.

pubmed:42701074.summary: This retrospective study of 788 bariatric surgery patients found that preoperative percent of excess weight loss was significantly associated with resolution of diabetes and hyperlipidemia during the immediate postoperative period (1-6 months). At 1 year, diabetes resolution was highest at 80.0%, followed by hypertension (61.1%), hyperlipidemia (53.3%), and obstructive sleep apnea (29.3%).

rank.reason: Human insomnia connectivity review; touches sleep-wake regulatory hubs but cross-sectional, not core animal/EEG focus.

pubmed:42701814.summary: This systematic review synthesized resting-state functional connectivity (rsFC) studies in insomnia disorder published from 2020 to July 2025. It found alterations in multiple brain networks and sleep-wake hubs compatible with hyperarousal, but methodological heterogeneity precluded quantitative pooling, and cross-sectional designs limit causal inference.

rank.topic: Movement behaviors and cognition in aging
rank.reason: Associations of sleep with cognition in older adults; broad human correlational study, tangential to mechanisms.

pubmed:42701867.summary: Cross-sectional analysis from the AGUEDA trial found no direct associations between 24-hour movement behaviors and cognition in older adults, but gray matter mean diffusivity (GMMD) moderated associations, particularly for episodic memory and light physical activity, indicating the importance of microstructural brain integrity.

rank.reason: Clinical epilepsy phenotype; EEG mentioned but disease-specific, not sleep regulation.

pubmed:42701350.summary: This international retrospective study of 17 patients with classic infantile Pompe disease found that epilepsy is part of the CNS phenotype, with seizures occurring predominantly after age 7 years. Most patients had EEG abnormalities, cognitive impairment, white matter changes, and elevated serum neurofilament light chain, and 70% became seizure-free on antiseizure medication.

rank.reason: Clinical OSA screening in kidney disease; no relevance to sleep homeostasis or neurophysiology.

pubmed:42700007.summary: This cross-sectional study of 40 dialysis patients with excessive daytime sleepiness found that over-hydration, assessed by body composition monitoring, was an independent predictor of obstructive sleep apnea severity, particularly in peritoneal dialysis patients. The Epworth Sleepiness Scale was suggested as a useful screening tool.

rank.reason: Case report; incidental OSA history, no sleep science content.

pubmed:42699905.summary: This case report describes a 55-year-old man with a giant benign esophageal schwannoma mimicking a mediastinal tumor, which was resected via subtotal esophagectomy with retrosternal gastric tube reconstruction. The tumor showed high FDG uptake on PET despite benign pathology, highlighting diagnostic challenges; the patient remained recurrence-free at 1 year postoperatively.

rank.reason: Sleep quality predictor of cognitive decline; human perioperative, unrelated to animal sleep regulation.

pubmed:42700994.summary: This prospective cohort study of 309 elderly patients undergoing single-port VATS lobectomy identified multidimensional perioperative predictors of delayed neurocognitive recovery (DNR). Higher Surgical Apgar Score was protective, while higher Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index and Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale scores were independent risk factors, with an AUC of 0.919.

rank.reason: Overnight lens wear; myopia treatment, no sleep neurophysiology.

pubmed:42699018.summary: This prospective study in Taiwan compared overnight orthokeratology in 15 teenagers and 53 adults with myopia over 9 months. Both groups achieved significant improvement in uncorrected visual acuity to approximately 20/20 and reduction of spherical equivalent to about 0.0 D, with minimal corneal staining and stable endothelial cell density, and returned to baseline by week 4 after discontinuation.

rank.topic: Brain dynamic audio stimulation for insomnia
rank.reason: EEG-based audio intervention but small pilot, subjective outcomes, not mechanistically informative.

pubmed:42698692.summary: This pilot feasibility study tested a 14-day Brain Dynamic Audio Stimulation (BDAS) intervention in healthcare professionals with subjective sleep disturbances. Results showed high retention and significant reductions in insomnia severity scores and sleep onset latency, with EEG changes suggesting improved sleep initiation.

rank.reason: Large epidemiological study with metabolic markers; broad associations, not mechanistic or suitable for transfer.

pubmed:42699646.summary: Using data from the China Kadoorie Biobank and UK Biobank, this study examined associations between sleep duration, metabolic markers, and mortality. It found that sleep duration was associated with specific lipid metabolites (e.g., lipoprotein subclasses, ketone bodies) which were also linked to all-cause and cause-specific mortality, suggesting a mediating role of lipid metabolism.

rank.topic: Deep TMS effects on QEEG in depression
rank.reason: EEG power and coherence changes; relevant spectral methods but in MDD, not sleep regulation.

pubmed:42700487.summary: This study examined the effects of deep transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) on quantitative EEG (QEEG) measures in 75 patients with major depressive disorder. After a 36-session protocol, depressive symptoms significantly reduced (82.6% response rate), along with decreased delta activity in the left prefrontal cortex, leftward frontal beta asymmetry shift, and improved coherence between left prefrontal and temporal lobes.

rank.reason: Occupational health survey; sleep disorders as outcome, no objective measures or mechanisms.

pubmed:42700071.summary: This cross-sectional study of 1540 Chinese emergency department nurses used latent profile analysis to identify three workplace violence exposure patterns (low-level, moderate multi-form, high multi-form) and machine learning to predict sleep disorders, which affected 59.3% of participants. Random forest achieved the highest predictive performance (AUC=0.624), with burnout and occupational characteristics contributing more to predictions than violence profiles.

rank.reason: Uses EEG measures but for interest profiling; no sleep relevance.

pubmed:42698853.summary: This study compared EEG-based vocational interest assessments with self-reported RIASEC profiles in 33 participants, finding strong overall convergence but discrepancies that led to different occupational recommendations, suggesting neurometrics can complement self-report measures.

rank.reason: EEG spectral modulation, but task-related motor; no sleep context.

pubmed:42698502.summary: This EEG study compared sensorimotor alpha rhythm modulation during motor imagery, electrical stimulation, and mirror visual feedback in 11 patients after peripheral nerve reconstruction and 21 healthy controls. Patients showed significant alpha suppression during electrical stimulation and mirror visual feedback, but not during motor imagery alone, suggesting multimodal rehabilitation may better facilitate cortical reorganization.

rank.reason: EEG feature changes longitudinally; valuable long-term recording concept but epilepsy focus, not sleep.

pubmed:42700753.summary: This post hoc analysis of data from a long-term RNS System treatment study in patients with drug-resistant focal epilepsy sought to define a clinically meaningful change in intracranial EEG long episode (LE) frequency. A LE reduction of ≥30% was associated with a ≥50% clinical seizure reduction (AUC=0.765), supporting LE reduction as a potential biomarker.

rank.reason: Case report; sleep disturbance mentioned as symptom, irrelevant.

pubmed:42699525.summary: The paper reports a case of a 70-year-old man with short bowel syndrome with intestinal failure after small-bowel volvulus, treated with teduglutide. Treatment led to complete weaning from parenteral nutrition, improved stool consistency and frequency, resolution of catheter-related bloodstream infections, and improved quality of life.

rank.reason: Clinical OSA with nocturnal BP/HRV; non-EEG, not mechanistic sleep regulation.

pubmed:42698248.summary: An observational study of hypertensive patients found that greater obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) severity, measured by AHI, was associated with higher nocturnal systolic blood pressure after adjustment, with trends toward reduced nocturnal blood pressure dipping and altered autonomic function.

rank.topic: Letter re: remimazolam and sleep quality
rank.reason: Correspondence piece; irrelevant to research interests.

pubmed:42699705.summary: This document is a response to a letter regarding a study on remimazolam versus propofol sedation and postoperative sleep quality after gastroscopy. It addresses comments about the original study.

rank.reason: Directly examines sleep expression in novel animal model with EEG/EOG and stress effects; highly relevant to comparative sleep regulation.

biorxiv:10.64898/2026.09.01.748758.summary: The study used miniature loggers to measure sleep in wild-caught Peninsular rock agama lizards (Psammophilus dorsalis) from urban and rural environments. Sleep characteristics were largely similar between populations, with urban individuals showing more consolidated daytime sleep bouts and marginally quicker arousal responses at night, while acute restraint stress did not affect sleep.

rank.reason: CFD modeling of upper airway; technical but unrelated to neurophysiology or sleep regulation dynamics.

pubmed:42701512.summary: Computational fluid dynamics simulations of the upper airway in children with adenoid hypertrophy showed that AH significantly reduced nasopharyngeal cross-sectional area, increasing pressure, flow velocity, and wall shear stress, while adenoidectomy restored airflow parameters to near-normal levels.

rank.reason: Clinical cross-sectional study on composite biomarkers for CKM phenotypes; unrelated to sleep neuroscience.

pubmed:42698609.summary: This cross-sectional study of 1,226 adults undergoing routine health examinations found that adverse cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) phenotype (stage >=2) was present in 58.56% of participants. The atherogenic index of plasma (AIP) and triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index showed high discrimination (AUC 0.87) for prevalent adverse CKM phenotype, with random forest achieving the best internal performance (AUC 0.89).

rank.reason: ERCP sedation study with processed EEG parameters; peripheral, but mentions EEG, minimal relevance.

pubmed:42699223.summary: In this open-label randomized controlled trial, 94 patients undergoing ERCP under dexmedetomidine-based sedation were randomized to nasal high flow (NHF) or low-flow oxygen. NHF significantly reduced opioid requirements (median pethidine dose 43.75 mg vs. 70.00 mg) while maintaining oxygenation and ventilation.

rank.topic: cognitive frailty models in heart failure
rank.reason: Systematic review on cognitive frailty models in CHF patients; no sleep component, very low relevance.

pubmed:42698449.summary: This systematic review evaluated models for identifying cognitive frailty in hospitalized older adults with chronic heart failure in China, finding eight cross-sectional studies with 20 models, all at high risk of bias. The models were diagnostic for prevalent cognitive frailty rather than prognostic, with limited external validation and none ready for clinical use.

rank.topic: Cortical dynamics across sleep and isolation
rank.reason: Directly relevant to NREM sleep and local network dynamics using human recordings and slices; provides concepts on rhythmic synchrony vs network integration, though human focus and lack of sleep homeostasis/EEG spectral analysis limit direct transfer.

biorxiv:10.64898/2026.09.02.748777.summary: The study compared cortical activity in humans across wakefulness, sleep, and isolated cortex slices, finding that isolating cortex increases gamma synchronization but reduces network integration and dimensionality. This suggests local circuits generate gamma while long-range inputs support diverse dynamics.

rank.reason: Broad clinical review on nutrition for athletes; only tangential mention of sleep and circadian rhythms.

pubmed:42703261.summary: This review discusses nutritional strategies to optimize recovery in overhead athletes after intense exercise, focusing on replenishing glycogen, repairing muscle, rehydrating, and addressing inflammation and sleep. It provides guidance on carbohydrate and fluid intake, protein synthesis, and meal timing to support recovery and immune function.

rank.topic: Employment predictors in spinal cord injury
rank.reason: Clinical/epidemiological study on employment; sleep disturbances only one variable, not relevant to sleep neuroscience.

pubmed:42703849.summary: Using random forest analysis on survey data from 538 individuals with spinal cord injury in South Korea, this study identified predictors of paid employment, including higher household income, younger age, higher self-efficacy, better quality of life, access to vocational rehabilitation, and absence of disability benefits. These findings can inform policies to improve employment opportunities.

rank.topic: Circadian gene expression in chronic kidney disease
rank.reason: Relevant to circadian-homeostatic interactions and rhythmic gene expression, but in renal tissue and disease model; provides methods for rhythmic analysis though not directly on sleep regulation.

pubmed:42703061.summary: This study performed time-series RNA-seq on kidneys from CKD mice, showing disrupted circadian transcriptome with acquired rhythmicity in immune-inflammatory genes and decreased rhythmicity in metabolic genes. Dapagliflozin partially restored core clock gene rhythms and improved renal function.

rank.reason: Military health construct, broad clinical; sleep is one aspect but not mechanistically relevant.

pubmed:42704257.summary: This scoping review systematically mapped the evidence for 'Operator Syndrome' in Special Operations Forces, identifying six sources. It found the construct is conceptually heterogeneous with no consensus definition, limited empirical support, and substantial overlap with other conditions such as mild traumatic brain injury and PTSD.

rank.reason: Clinical OSA diagnostics in children; focuses on morphology, not sleep regulation or animal neuroscience.

pubmed:42703366.summary: Cross-sectional study of 205 children with moderate-to-severe OSA found that cephalometric indices (FMA and hyoid bone distance) were independently associated with OAHI, but with weak explanatory power. Acoustic pharyngometry measures correlated with height and FMIA, indicating cephalometry provides additional endotypic information.

rank.reason: Uses EEG features and classification, possibly transferable methods for spectral analysis but in clinical psychiatric context, not sleep.

pubmed:42702788.summary: The study introduced 25 EEG features and evaluated their diagnostic utility for affective disorders using two resting-state datasets. It identified biomarkers with strong discriminative power and discussed challenges in EEG-based diagnosis and multimodal integration.

rank.reason: Applies qEEG spectral and connectivity metrics to delirium endotypes, providing methods for EEG spectral analysis and severity continuum, but not directly sleep regulation.

pubmed:42702808.summary: This observational cohort study used quantitative EEG in stroke patients, finding that connectivity metrics detect poststroke delirium with high accuracy and correlate with inflammatory biomarkers. This suggests EEG connectivity captures delirium endotypes beyond clinical phenotype.

rank.topic: DRP-1 and circadian rhythms in PCOS
rank.reason: Links mitochondrial dynamics and circadian rhythms, but in PCOS context; theoretical connection to circadian disruption.

pubmed:42704293.summary: This review explores the role of Dynamin-related protein 1 (DRP-1) in mitochondrial fission and its potential link between circadian rhythm disruption and polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS), particularly involving oxidative stress and hormonal imbalances. It highlights DRP-1 as a possible therapeutic target for addressing mitochondrial and circadian dysfunction in PCOS.

rank.topic: Source EEG network dynamics in SSD
rank.reason: Longitudinal source EEG study examining spectral power and network efficiency, providing methods in source-localized EEG and recovery trajectories, but in somatic symptom disorder, not sleep.

pubmed:42702819.summary: This 6-month longitudinal source EEG study in 83 patients with somatic symptom disorder (SSD) and 80 controls found persistent reduction in gamma-band global efficiency in SSD, while clinical improvement was associated with reorganization of nodal efficiency in the left central sensorimotor region and longitudinal changes in thalamic spectral power. These findings suggest multilayered neurobiological changes underlie SSD recovery.

rank.topic: Lighting effects on diurnal rodent rhythms
rank.reason: Uses a diurnal rodent model to test how lighting conditions affect daily activity rhythms, highly relevant to circadian-homeostatic interactions and environmental effects on sleep regulation; strong methodological fit.

pubmed:42704063.summary: This study compared circadian and physiological effects of different lighting conditions in diurnal Nile grass rats, finding that daylight-equivalent lighting produced stronger entrainment than fluorescent indoor light. Fluorescent light increased diabetic rate and reduced sperm motility, suggesting health consequences of circadian disruption.

rank.topic: Hybrid BCI system using SSVEP and sEMG
rank.reason: Brain-computer interface technology; unrelated to sleep neuroscience.

pubmed:42703192.summary: This paper presents a hybrid brain-computer interface combining steady-state visual evoked potentials and surface electromyography to encode 480 targets. In online experiments, it achieved an average classification accuracy of 84.55% and an information transfer rate of 260.07 bits/min, demonstrating high performance for large command sets.

rank.reason: Analyzes EEG multiscale entropy in ASD; uses complexity measures and movie viewing, but not sleep-related.

biorxiv:10.64898/2026.09.01.747412.summary: This EEG study in adults with autism spectrum disorder (ASD, n=47) and typically developing controls (n=40) found reduced multiscale entropy (MSE) at longer time scales in ASD across rest and movie-viewing conditions, which was associated with higher social affect scores on the ADOS-2. Event-related analyses showed attenuated differentiation of MSE between social and non-social movie windows in ASD, indicating reduced neural complexity relevant to social processing.

rank.reason: Characterizes circadian variation in physical performance, relevant to circadian-homeostatic interactions but in humans and exercise, not sleep regulation directly.

pubmed:42703154.summary: In a randomized crossover study of 15 healthy adults, short-duration cycling performance and handgrip strength peaked in the late afternoon/early evening (around 18:00), with significant time-of-day variation across the waking day. Physiological states, including tympanic temperature, sleepiness, blood glucose, and lactate, also varied diurnally, indicating time-of-day as a relevant factor in exercise testing.

rank.topic: Eating and lifestyle in shift workers
rank.reason: Survey on shift workers' diet and sleep duration; broad epidemiology, some relevance to circadian disruption but not mechanistic.

pubmed:42702548.summary: This study compared eating habits and lifestyle characteristics between shift and daytime workers using data from the 2018 Japan National Health and Nutrition Survey (n=1,814). Both male and female shift workers consumed significantly less fish and shellfish and had shorter sleep duration, while female shift workers also consumed less milk and dairy products, suggesting targeted dietary and lifestyle adjustments for shift workers.

rank.topic: Genetic risk and social jetlag in obesity
rank.reason: Links genetic risk score to social jetlag and obesity, relevant to circadian misalignment, but cross-sectional human data with limited depth.

pubmed:42703854.summary: In 223 Turkish adults, social jetlag was associated with higher BMI, but this association was attenuated after adjusting for a genetic risk score based on FTO, MC4R, and TCF7L2, and those with more risk alleles had higher BMI. Among participants with social jetlag, metabolic genetic risk was positively correlated with BMI and body fat measures, suggesting an interaction between circadian misalignment and genetic obesity susceptibility.

rank.reason: Clinical pharmacokinetic study in sedated patients with OSA; not relevant to sleep regulation mechanisms.

pubmed:42703687.summary: This study characterized remimazolam pharmacokinetics in volunteers with different obesity levels and obstructive sleep apnea severity using a population pharmacokinetic model. Total body weight significantly affected clearance and metabolite volume, but obstructive sleep apnea severity did not; the study recommends lean/ideal body weight for induction and adjusted body weight for maintenance in class 2/3 obesity.

rank.topic: DISE and HOBE in obstructive sleep apnea
rank.reason: Clinical study assessing anatomical correlates of positional therapy; focuses on upper airway, not sleep regulation.

pubmed:42703892.summary: This study assessed associations between drug-induced sleep endoscopy (DISE) findings and rhinomanometric parameters with response to 30° head-of-bed elevation (HOBE) in obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) patients. HOBE significantly reduced AHI, with epiglottic and tongue base collapse scores strongly correlated with improvement, suggesting DISE may help characterize positional responsivity, though results are hypothesis-generating.

rank.reason: Epidemiological study on 24-h movement behaviors including sleep, but outcome is academic performance in children, far from research interests.

pubmed:42702858.summary: Using longitudinal data from 3973 Australian children, this study found that each additional wave of adherence to 24-hour movement guidelines (ages 6-13) was associated with higher Year 9 numeracy and reading scores. Adherence at exposure wave was linked to subsequent reading performance.

rank.topic: Occupational therapy sleep intervention for veterans
rank.reason: Applied CBT-I intervention with occupational focus; clinical and not mechanistic, though relevant to sleep disturbance.

pubmed:42701328.summary: This pilot study tested a 5-week occupational therapy-led modified cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) program for Montana veterans with self-reported sleep disturbances. Participants showed improvements in sleep, occupational performance, and mental health, with high feasibility and acceptability, suggesting OT-led CBT-I may be effective in community settings.

rank.reason: Rare genetic syndrome with developmental delay; no link to sleep regulation or neuroscience methods relevant to the researcher's focus.

pubmed:42702753.summary: This paper presents a case of a patient with global developmental delay and microtia carrying a de novo pathogenic DHX30 missense variant, along with a scoping review of 51 individuals with DHX30-related neurodevelopmental disorder. The review confirms common features such as motor delay, intellectual disability, hypotonia, and feeding difficulties, and suggests that microtia may be a novel manifestation.

rank.reason: RLS is a sleep disorder, and autonomic dysfunction may relate to sleep fragmentation mechanisms, but the focus is clinical and not directly on the researcher's core questions.

pubmed:42702919.summary: This systematic review examined evidence for organ-specific autonomic disturbances in primary restless legs syndrome (RLS), analyzing 41 studies comparing RLS patients and controls. Findings showed heterogeneous but convergent evidence of multidomain autonomic dysfunction involving cardiovascular, endothelial, thermoregulatory, gastrointestinal, genitourinary, and sexual domains, with dopaminergic therapy improving some indices.

rank.reason: Endocrine disorder affecting sleep indirectly, but clinical focus far from animal sleep neuroscience.

pubmed:42701317.summary: This clinical review discusses the diagnosis and management of Cushing's syndrome in older adults, highlighting differences in presentation, test interpretation, and treatment. It emphasizes a practical approach that accounts for age-related comorbidities, frailty, and functional status to avoid both underdiagnosis and overdiagnosis.

rank.topic: Sleep disorders in Cri du Chat
rank.reason: Rare genetic syndrome with sleep problems; descriptive clinical study without mechanistic insight useful for the researcher.

pubmed:42702178.summary: Questionnaire-based study of 70 adults with Cri du Chat syndrome found high prevalence of poor sleep quality (49%) and insomnia symptoms (35.7%), with sleep maintenance disturbances most frequent (47.1%). Older age and epilepsy were associated with more severe sleep problems.

rank.reason: Case report mentioning sleep improvement with naltrexone; peripheral to core sleep neuroscience topics.

pubmed:42704315.summary: Case report of a 10-year-old girl with ASD and Helsmoortel-van der Aa syndrome and severe self-injury, where naltrexone reduced SIB by >50% within 4 weeks and improved irritability and sleep. This suggests naltrexone may be a useful adjunctive treatment.

rank.reason: Cross-sectional study on trauma and sleep quality in adolescents; not mechanistic and far from animal models.

pubmed:42703223.summary: This cross-sectional study of 1,579 adolescent earthquake survivors in Adıyaman, Türkiye, found that smokers had lower perceived social support. Perceived social support showed weak negative correlations with poor sleep quality and insomnia, with the strongest negative correlations for family support.

rank.reason: General health survey in medical students; sleep is one factor, not relevant to the researcher's focus.

pubmed:42703387.summary: This cross-sectional study of 250 female medical students found a 75.2% prevalence of premenstrual syndrome. PMS was significantly associated with reduced productivity, increased mental stress, and greater analgesic use.

rank.reason: Essay on social media addiction; mentions sleep problems in broad human context, no relevance to sleep neuroscience research.

pubmed:42704232.summary: This note examines the harms of adolescent social media use, drawing parallels to addiction, and argues for regulation of addictive design features like algorithmic recommendations and infinite scroll rather than content. It reviews current legal frameworks and proposes legislative approaches to protect minors, acknowledging challenges such as First Amendment and Section 230.

rank.reason: Clinical overlap of OSA with COPD; general sleep apnea research, not mechanistic or computationally focused on the researcher's interests.

pubmed:42703559.summary: A bibliometric analysis of 1239 publications on COPD-OSA overlap syndrome (2000-2025) using LDA identified 10 latent topics, showing a shift from disease coexistence to multimorbidity and individualized management. International collaboration remains low.

rank.reason: Includes sleep as one health behaviour for screening tool development; no relevance to basic sleep regulation research.

pubmed:42703021.summary: In nominal group technique workshops, Australian primary health care practitioners identified and prioritized key features for a child health behavior screening tool, including clear results and next steps and question design. They also highlighted needs for practitioner training and resources to support implementation, providing guidance for developing an acceptable screening tool.

rank.reason: Focuses on REM-specific HFO chains and hippocampal-cortical reactivation, adjacent to NREM sigma/slow-wave interest but lacks direct NREM duration or homeostasis focus.

pubmed:42704658.summary: This study in rodents identifies prefrontal cortical high-frequency oscillation (HFO) chains during REM sleep that phase-modulate with theta oscillations and coordinate sparse hippocampal-cortical reactivation of spatial memories, contrasting with NREM ripples. A cortical network model incorporating acetylcholine effects reproduces these distinct REM and NREM activity patterns, linking REM HFOs to memory consolidation.

rank.topic: Early-life GABA blockade and sleep deprivation
rank.reason: Uses 24-h SD but investigates developmental GABA manipulation and anxiety/cognition, far from mechanistic sleep regulation or rebound trajectories.

pubmed:42704577.summary: This study in male rats found that early-life transient blockade of GABA-A receptors with bicuculline prevented cognitive deficits and anxiety-like behaviors induced by 24-hr sleep deprivation in adulthood, and restored hippocampal antioxidant enzyme activities and MDA levels. This suggests a developmental role of early GABAergic signaling in resilience to sleep loss.

rank.reason: Human clinical pain prediction, unrelated to sleep regulation or animal neuroscience core topics.

pubmed:42704736.summary: In a prospective cohort of breast cancer surgery patients, higher preoperative resting-state frontal gamma power and connectivity were associated with clinically significant chronic postoperative pain at 3 months. The study suggests frontal gamma activity may reflect baseline neurophysiological vulnerability to chronic pain.

rank.reason: Review on wearables for mood phenotyping, general human sleep/circadian but no direct relevance to animal sleep research or mechanisms.

pubmed:42704686.summary: This narrative review discusses how wearable sensors can monitor sleep, circadian rhythms, and hormonal changes to phenotype perinatal mood disorders, potentially enabling earlier diagnosis and personalized interventions. It highlights the need for continuous monitoring to differentiate risk and improve maternal well-being.

rank.reason: Epidemiological study in women on psychosocial factors and sleep, too broad and distant from quantitative sleep regulation.

pubmed:42704517.summary: This study analyzed data from 31,443 women in the Sister Study and found that maladaptive coping strategies mediated the relationship between perceived differential treatment based on race-ethnicity and poor sleep quality and insomnia symptoms, particularly among non-Hispanic Black and White women. The findings suggest that addressing maladaptive coping may reduce sleep disturbances.

rank.reason: Reviews circadian clocks in skin, tangential to circadian-sleep interactions, but no relevance to EEG/EMG or sleep homeostasis.

pubmed:42704419.summary: This narrative review summarizes evidence that skin has intrinsic circadian clocks regulating physiology and disease processes, and highlights chronodermatology as a promising approach. However, it notes most therapeutic applications require more prospective human trials before clinical recommendation.

rank.reason: Clinical OSA severity and mortality, human cohort, unrelated to basic mechanistic or computational sleep research.

pubmed:42704465.summary: This study analyzed NHANES data (n=9,797) and a clinical dataset (n=258) to show that higher EASIX levels are associated with increased all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in OSA, and significantly correlated with OSA severity indices (AHI, ODI). Machine learning models highlighted EASIX as a key predictor, suggesting its potential as a biomarker for risk stratification.

rank.reason: Occupational health RCT using self-reported sleep, clinical and methodological irrelevant to animal sleep neuroscience.

pubmed:42704835.summary: This randomized controlled trial with 60 male börek workers found that adding a 12-week supervised, equipment-free exercise program to ergonomics education significantly reduced musculoskeletal symptoms compared to education alone, with improvements also in sleep and burnout. The study calls for objective confirmation due to self-reported outcomes.

rank.reason: Human biomarker study, clinical insomnia but no connection to EEG spectral dynamics or animal models.

pubmed:42704542.summary: This cross-sectional study of hemodialysis patients found that higher plasma BDNF levels were associated with poor sleep quality only in those not using hypnotic medications, and BDNF levels were positively correlated with hypnotic medication use. The authors suggest BDNF may be a biomarker for insomnia in hemodialysis patients not taking hypnotics.

rank.reason: Directly investigates a cortical circuit (L6b) involved in EEG oscillations and responses to orexin, using chronic EEG in mice and sleep deprivation, highly relevant to sleep regulation and state-dependent dynamics.

pubmed:42706848.summary: The study silenced a subset of cortical layer 6b neurons in mice and found reduced EEG power, particularly in NREM sleep, and a slowing of theta frequency during wake and REM sleep. The response to orexin A was altered, suggesting L6b neurons regulate state-dependent brain oscillations.

rank.reason: Examines local slow-wave dynamics and OFF-periods in prelimbic cortex predicting resilience to stress in mice, relevant to local sleep regulation and EEG measures, though more focused on stress than sleep homeostasis.

pubmed:42705913.summary: The study recorded prelimbic cortex activity in mice before and after social defeat stress, finding that resilient mice had stronger coupling between neuronal OFF-periods and slow-waves at baseline and showed reorganization of OFF-period patterns after stress. This suggests a capacity for flexible network redistribution during NREM sleep predicts resilience.

rank.reason: Broad clinical review on circadian rhythms and AD, mostly molecular and clinical, with no direct relevance to sleep homeostasis or animal EEG work.

pubmed:42708270.summary: This review examines the interplay between circadian rhythm disruption and Alzheimer's disease, highlighting that circadian gene dysregulation exacerbates tau and amyloid pathology, and discusses therapeutic approaches like light therapy and melatonin. It emphasizes the need for integrated and personalized circadian-based therapies.

rank.reason: Human EEG study on psychedelics, unrelated to sleep regulation or animal research; findings on signal complexity may be methodologically interesting but not directly applicable.

pubmed:42705377.summary: EEG recordings in 13 healthy participants under intravenous DMT revealed reduced functional connectivity, increased signal complexity in beta/gamma bands, and decreased complexity in delta/theta/alpha bands. DMT also increased arousal and well-being correlates, supporting the entropic brain theory.

rank.topic: Infraslow oscillations in sleep and AD
rank.reason: Analyzes NREM sleep sigma power infraslow oscillations in humans, linking to glymphatic and LC function; concept could be relevant to sleep microarchitecture, but human AD focus and no direct mechanistic link to core questions.

pubmed:42708477.summary: The study analyzed NREM sleep EEG in Alzheimer's disease (AD) participants and controls, finding reduced infraslow oscillation (ISO) peak amplitude in AD with preserved frequency and bandwidth. ISO amplitude trended with Aβ42/40, and bandwidth was associated with NfL, suggesting ISO may link sleep and AD pathology.

rank.reason: Clinical study on postoperative delirium prediction with deep learning, not related to sleep regulation or animal models.

pubmed:42707129.summary: This study developed an interpretable deep learning framework using intraoperative EEG to predict postoperative delirium with high accuracy, identifying a frontal 2-12 Hz oscillation biomarker. The biomarker was validated externally, supporting its use for early warning and individualized care.

rank.reason: Reviews MCH role in sleep and memory, including REM sleep effects; relevant as background on arousal and memory systems, but not directly about sleep homeostasis or quantitative modeling.

pubmed:42707409.summary: This mini-review summarizes studies on melanin-concentrating hormone (MCH) in memory, noting its complex role in promoting consolidation, inducing forgetting during REM sleep, or negatively regulating memory formation. It also discusses emerging links to Alzheimer's disease, including therapeutic potential and effects on sleep architecture.

rank.reason: Drosophila circadian study on timeless affecting aging and cardiac function via exercise; limited relevance to mammalian sleep regulation and EEG.

pubmed:42706483.summary: Using Drosophila, this study showed that muscle-specific knockdown of Timeless accelerates age-related circadian and cardiac dysfunction, while overexpression delays it. A 4-week endurance exercise regimen counteracted the effects of knockdown and further improved outcomes in aged flies, suggesting exercise acts through Timeless upregulation.

rank.reason: Human EEG study on handedness and social behavior, completely outside sleep neuroscience.

pubmed:42704939.summary: In a Go/NoGo task with EEG, this study investigated how sex and handedness affect neural signatures of cooperative and competitive behavior, finding that accuracy was higher in males, and response times were faster in the enemy condition, with some EEG differences consistent with the evolutionarily stable strategy hypothesis.

rank.reason: Systematic review of EEG functional connectivity in ADHD; not relevant to sleep or animal EEG.

pubmed:42705510.summary: This systematic review synthesized 37 EEG functional connectivity studies in ADHD, finding convergent patterns of reduced posterior integration with frontal compensation and altered network organization. These EEG findings parallel fMRI evidence, supporting EEG as a translational tool for ADHD.

rank.reason: Mapping of cholinergic neurons in tree shrew vs. mouse; may be useful for anatomy but lacks direct connection to sleep electrophysiology.

pubmed:42706791.summary: This study systematically mapped the whole-brain distribution and morphology of choline acetyltransferase-immunoreactive (ChAT-ir) neurons in the tree shrew and compared them with those in mice, revealing key interspecies differences such as absence of cortical ChAT-ir neurons in the tree shrew and higher density in specific subcortical nuclei. The findings provide a structural framework for studying cholinergic roles in neural functions.

rank.topic: Local slow wave modulation by auditory stimuli
rank.reason: Corrigendum to a paper on local modulation of sleep slow waves, directly relevant to neural mechanisms of slow wave activity and plasticity; likely of high interest despite being a correction.

pubmed:42706001.summary: This is a published erratum for the article 'Local modulation of sleep slow waves depends on timing between auditory stimuli'. It contains no new scientific content.

rank.topic: Prediction of cognitive impairment in Parkinson's
rank.reason: Clinical study combining blood and sleep questionnaires; not relevant to basic sleep research or EEG techniques.

pubmed:42706737.summary: This cross-sectional study of 347 Parkinson's disease patients developed a leakage-free nested modeling framework combining routine blood indicators and sleep questionnaires to identify cognitive impairment, achieving a test-set AUC of 0.943 in the full logistic regression model, which significantly outperformed a clinical baseline model.

rank.reason: Review on nasal physiology in pregnancy, tangential to sleep but no direct relevance to the researcher's interests.

pubmed:42705916.summary: This narrative review discusses the physiological changes in nasal breathing during pregnancy, including hormonal effects on nasal mucosa, and explores potential consequences of nasal obstruction such as sleep-disordered breathing and adverse pregnancy outcomes. It also reviews interventions like pranayama and nasal dilators, noting that many require further study in pregnant populations.

rank.reason: Review of PSG characteristics in menopause OSA, clinical population; low relevance to basic sleep regulation.

pubmed:42706212.summary: This review summarizes the polysomnographic characteristics of perimenopausal women with OSA, identifying a unique pattern of REM-predominant hypopneas and intermittent hypoxia linked to cognitive decline. It advocates for multidimensional assessment beyond AHI for early identification and management.

rank.reason: Human behavioral study on sleep inertia, not measuring EEG or mechanistic insights, though sleep inertia relates to sleep-wake transitions.

pubmed:42707609.summary: This randomized controlled trial evaluated cognitive stimulation and physiological dynamization as countermeasures for sleep inertia after normal and recovery sleep. Physiological dynamization significantly reduced reaction time and lapses within 20 minutes post-awakening, suggesting it is a promising intervention.

rank.reason: Epidemiological study on circadian syndrome and frailty in elderly; no mechanistic or methodological value for animal research.

pubmed:42705508.summary: This longitudinal study of 7330 Chinese adults found that circadian syndrome (CircS) at baseline was associated with higher risks of moderate-rising and high-stable frailty trajectories, and that a greater number of CircS components was linked to faster increases in frailty index over time.

rank.reason: Human study of time-of-day effects on subjective states and cognition; some relevance to circadian performance, but no EEG or mechanistic depth.

pubmed:42708375.summary: The study assessed subjective states and cognitive performance at multiple times of day in both laboratory and real work settings. Results showed a post-lunch decline in sleepiness and vitality, and cognitive performance varied by task, with sustained attention best in the morning and working memory better in the afternoon.

rank.reason: Clinical study on tDCS effects on negative symptoms using TMS-EEG; not related to sleep regulation.

pubmed:42705493.summary: This study combined TMS-EEG and a randomized double-blind trial to show that HD-tDCS targeting the left DLPFC improves negative symptoms in schizophrenia, with N100 normalization as a potential biomarker. The improvement in negative symptoms was specifically associated with N100 changes, suggesting restoration of cortical inhibition.

rank.reason: Environmental epidemiology cohort study, irrelevant to sleep neuroscience.

pubmed:42705027.summary: In a UK Biobank cohort of 410,207 participants, long-term ambient benzene exposure was associated with increased risks of psychiatric disorders, including multiple psychiatric disorders, with accelerated biological aging partially mediating the associations.

rank.reason: Broad dental review with a small sleep medicine section; not relevant to basic/computational sleep neuroscience.

pubmed:42705955.summary: This annual review by the American Academy of Restorative Dentistry summarizes selected 2025 dental literature across multiple disciplines including prosthodontics, implant dentistry, operative dentistry, and others. It aims to update restorative dentists on new materials, technologies, and evidence-based practices.

rank.reason: Mentions sleep data from wearables but focuses on legal/insurance issues; no relevance to sleep regulation mechanisms.

pubmed:42704992.summary: This narrative review examines the evidentiary value and medico-legal limitations of wearable-derived data in insurance and legal medicine, concluding that such data cannot independently establish disability or credibility and require cautious, clinically contextualized interpretation.

rank.reason: rs-fMRI in human development; not animal EEG/EMG sleep research, though could be tangentially related to brain network development.

pubmed:42705061.summary: This narrative review synthesizes human resting-state fMRI studies from the fetal period through infancy, highlighting hierarchical functional network development with early stabilization of sensorimotor systems and prolonged refinement of higher-order association systems, and associations with prematurity, early environments, and later neurodevelopmental outcomes.

rank.reason: Autoimmune hair loss; sleep disorders mentioned as contributing factor but not a focus on sleep neuroscience.

pubmed:42706968.summary: This integrative review summarizes the pathophysiology of alopecia areata, including CD8+NKG2D+ T cell activation and loss of follicular immune privilege, and discusses conventional and emerging therapies such as JAK inhibitors, biologics, and regenerative approaches with promising initial findings.

rank.reason: Autonomic measures during sleep segments; method for HRV could be transferable but focus on cardiac patients not sleep regulation.

pubmed:42706354.summary: This study evaluated the reliability of short-term heart rate variability (HRV) measurements from 48-h Holter recordings in patients with non-permanent atrial fibrillation, finding poor absolute reliability (limits of agreement up to several hundred percent) and suggesting limited use for individual-level clinical interpretation.

rank.reason: Clinical case series on children with severe OSA; not relevant to basic sleep homeostasis or computational modeling.

pubmed:42706068.summary: This case series describes the multidisciplinary management of three children with extremely severe obstructive sleep apnea and multisystem damage, all of whom underwent tonsillectomy and adenoidectomy after stabilization and had complete symptomatic relief at one-year follow-up.

rank.reason: Wearable-derived sleep and cardiovascular outcomes, stratification by baseline performance; adjacent to sleep regulation but in humans and product-focused, not animal neuroscience.

medrxiv:10.64898/2026.08.31.26361834.summary: In an open-label study of 171 adults, a temperature-controlled sleep surface increased total sleep time and improved overnight cardiovascular measures, with the largest gains observed in those with the poorest baseline sleep. Stratification by baseline performance revealed significant improvements in sleep efficiency, REM, deep sleep, and HRV in the most deficient quartiles.

rank.reason: Opioid toxicity; no connection to sleep neuroscience.

medrxiv:10.64898/2026.09.04.26362234.summary: This observational study analyzed Canadian death investigation data from 2016-2017 to identify signs and substances associated with naloxone administration in acute drug toxicity deaths. Naloxone was administered to 45% of decedents, more often when opioids contributed to death, and was associated with classic opioid toxicity signs; when opioids did not contribute, opioid or stimulant detection was associated with administration.

rank.reason: Parkinson's biomarkers; no sleep focus, though sleep issues may co-occur but not relevant to core questions.

pubmed:42707903.summary: This retrospective study compared DaT SPECT imaging and phosphorylated alpha-synuclein skin biopsy in 86 patients with diagnostically uncertain parkinsonism. Combined testing increased sensitivity to 95.6% but reduced specificity to 59.9%, with 30.8% discordance, suggesting these biomarkers provide complementary information supporting the dual-origin model of alpha-synuclein propagation.

rank.topic: human hippocampal NREM theta and memory
rank.reason: Human study on hippocampal CA1 theta during NREM and memory consolidation; tangential to animal sleep homeostasis and spectral dynamics, but not directly relevant to core interests.

biorxiv:10.64898/2026.09.02.748785.summary: This study on patients with transient global amnesia (TGA) found that hippocampal CA1 lesions impair sleep-dependent memory consolidation and reduce NREM theta power, which predicted consolidation improvements. Other NREM markers like spindles were unaffected, suggesting theta power reflects hippocampal integrity.

rank.reason: Animal study with EEG/EMG-based sleep measures including NREMS recovery, REMS, and bout duration; relevant to fragmentation and recovery, but specific to drug exposure not core interests.

biorxiv:10.64898/2026.09.02.748951.summary: This preprint study compared chronic fentanyl and xylazine exposure, alone and combined, in male and female mice. Combined exposure produced distinct sex-dependent alterations in sleep architecture and exacerbated respiratory depression, particularly in males, while increasing peripheral FGF21 levels.

rank.reason: Clinical intervention study in humans on sleep quality after surgery; not relevant to basic/computational sleep neuroscience or animal models.

pubmed:42709244.summary: This quasi-experimental study in ICU patients after hepatocellular carcinoma resection found that inhaled lavender essential oil aromatherapy significantly improved sleep quality and reduced pain and anxiety compared to usual care, as measured by validated scales.

rank.topic: Sleep deprivation effects on memory in mice
rank.reason: Uses a short sleep deprivation protocol and NOR task, but focus is on cognitive deficits and inflammation, not sleep homeostasis or recovery dynamics central to the researcher's interests.

pubmed:42714005.summary: This protocol describes a rapid workflow for modeling sleep deprivation-induced recognition memory deficits in mice using a 5-hour gentle-handling sleep deprivation after novel object recognition training. The workflow links behavioral outcomes to hippocampal inflammatory and oxidative stress biomarkers, emphasizing standardization and reproducibility.

rank.topic: Sleep spindle suppression of cortical excitability
rank.reason: Examines NREM spindle dynamics and GABAergic inhibition, relevant to spectral dynamics and NREM mechanisms, but primarily human TMS/EEG study, less aligned with animal sleep homeostasis.

biorxiv:10.64898/2026.09.03.748984.summary: This study used real-time EEG-triggered transcranial magnetic stimulation to test whether sleep spindle-related suppression of corticospinal excitability is mediated by GABA-Aergic inhibition. They found that spindles suppress corticospinal excitability without altering short-interval intracortical inhibition, suggesting distinct contributions of vigilance states and slow oscillations.

rank.reason: Focuses on hearing loss mechanisms, not directly on sleep regulation or SWA rebound; peripheral auditory effects are tangential to core research questions.

pubmed:42711899.summary: This study establishes a dose-dependent association between sleep disturbance severity and hearing loss in patients, and uses a mouse model to show that acute sleep deprivation causes persistent high-frequency hearing loss via cochlear synaptopathy. The mechanism involves transient oxidative stress initiating chronic neuroinflammation that suppresses BK channels, and antioxidant or BK channel opener treatment prevents the deficits.

rank.topic: Integrative review of sleep and circadian rhythms
rank.reason: Broad review covering circadian-homeostatic interactions and neural synchrony, providing useful background but not novel mechanistic insights or methods.

pubmed:42711021.summary: This review integrates mechanisms of sleep, circadian rhythms, chronobiology, and neural synchrony, detailing how the suprachiasmatic nucleus, clock gene feedback loops, and thalamocortical circuits coordinate brain function. It also highlights therapeutic avenues like chronotherapy and AI-based sleep analysis, emphasizing the intersection of chronobiology and neuroscience.

rank.reason: Discusses sleep depth instability and biomarkers like SWA and spindles, but focused on human insomnia, less relevant to animal models of sleep homeostasis.

pubmed:42711022.summary: This review develops a phenotype-informed framework for insomnia, distinguishing clinical presentations from mechanistic dimensions and biomarker domains. It reviews neurocognitive biomarkers, electrophysiological and sleep microstructure markers, and multimodal approaches, concluding that no single biomarker is sufficient and that integrative phenotyping can guide individualized treatment.

rank.reason: Applied machine learning for sleep staging from ECG, not relevant to EEG dynamics or sleep regulation questions.

pubmed:42711831.summary: This paper proposes SleepECGNet, a dual soft attention network for automatic sleep staging using single-lead ECG signals.
